choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) immediate (B) unnoticed (C) predicted 근거 ❶❷❼❿ 해설: (A) ❷ 새 기술의 분명한 측면은 알아차린다, ❼ 단기적이고 분명한 영향 → 즉각적인(immediate). delayed(지연된)는 반대. (B) ❶ 날마다 뚜렷하 게 보이지 않는 변화를 놓친다 → 눈에 띄지 않는(unnoticed). celebrated(찬양받는)는 반대. (C) ❿ 예상되지 못했고 예견하기도 어려웠다 → 예측되는 (predicted) 일이 드물다. ignored를 넣으면 ‘미리 무시되는 일이 드물다’가 되어 논지와 어긋남. 요약문 해석: 새로운 기술은 그것의 (A) 즉각적인 이점으로 평가되는 경향이 있는 반면, 그것이 일상생활에 가져오는 점진적인 변화는 (B) 눈에 띄지 않은 채 지나가며, 이것이 그 장기적 영향이 미리 (C) 예측되는 일이 드문 이유이다.
choice.psg: ❶ When we focus on the obvious aspects of media, we miss the changes that accumulate over time but are not apparent day to day. ❷ Most of us notice the obvious aspects of a new medium or technology while missing the more subtle aspects. ❸ Take, for example, the microwave oven. ❹ It was introduced in the early 1980s and revolutionized food preparation. ❺ Traditionally, one person spent the better part of an afternoon fixing an evening meal for a family. ❻ Now, it was possible to prepare foods very quickly, and this shortening of preparation time was liberating for the cooks in the family, most of whom tended to be women. ❼ But the short-term, obvious implications of greater convenience made it easy to overlook the long-term implications of no longer having one person fix food for the family to eat together at an evening meal. ❽ As time went on, fewer and fewer families sat down together to eat dinner. ❾ Meals that took a long time to prepare became a luxury of the past, except perhaps for special occasions. ❿ The effects of the microwave oven on family life were not anticipated and would have been difficult to foresee.
choice.body: New technologies tend to be judged by their (A)________ benefits, while the gradual changes they bring to everyday life go (B)________, which is why their long-term effects are rarely (C)________ in advance.

(C) ❽ 점점 더 적은 가족이 함께 둘러앉았다 → 모이다(gathered). ‘fewer families refused(거부하는 가족이 줄었다)’는 정반대 의미. 요약문 해석: 조리 시간을 크게 (A) 줄임으로써 전자레인지는 가족 내 요리사들을 해방시켰지만, 이 분명한 이득은 숨겨진 대가를 (B) 가렸다. 시간이 흐르 면서 저녁을 함께 먹기 위해 (C) 모이는 가족이 줄어든 것이다.
choice.psg: ❶ When we focus on the obvious aspects of media, we miss the changes that accumulate over time but are not apparent day to day. ❷ Most of us notice the obvious aspects of a new medium or technology while missing the more subtle aspects. ❸ Take, for example, the microwave oven. ❹ It was introduced in the early 1980s and revolutionized food preparation. ❺ Traditionally, one person spent the better part of an afternoon fixing an evening meal for a family. ❻ Now, it was possible to prepare foods very quickly, and this shortening of preparation time was liberating for the cooks in the family, most of whom tended to be women. ❼ But the short-term, obvious implications of greater convenience made it easy to overlook the long-term implications of no longer having one person fix food for the family to eat together at an evening meal. ❽ As time went on, fewer and fewer families sat down together to eat dinner. ❾ Meals that took a long time to prepare became a luxury of the past, except perhaps for special occasions. ❿ The effects of the microwave oven on family life were not anticipated and would have been difficult to foresee.
choice.body: By greatly (A)________ cooking time, the microwave oven freed family cooks, yet this obvious gain (B)________ a hidden cost: over time, fewer families (C)________ to eat dinner together.

choice.stem: 위 글의 내용으로부터 추론할 수 없는 것을 고르시오.
opt: Women were the main reason that the microwave oven became popular in the 1980s.
People can be so impressed by a technology’s convenience that they ignore its future costs.
Changes caused by technology can build up gradually without being clearly seen at first.
The microwave oven contributed to a decline in families eating dinner together.
Before the microwave oven, making dinner for a family could take up much of an afternoon.
choice.ex: ❻은 준비 시간 단축이 ‘대부분 여성이었던 가족 내 요리사들’을 해방시켰다고 할 뿐, 여성이 전자레인지 보급(인기)의 원인이었다는 내용은 없다(본문의 두 정보를 엮은 거짓 인과). ① 근거 없음(정답) — 여성들이 1980년대에 전자레인지가 인기를 얻은 주된 이유였다. ② 근거 ❼ — 사람들은 기술의 편리함에 너무 감명을 받아 그것의 미래 비용을 무시할 수 있다. ③ 근거 ❶ — 기술이 일으킨 변화는 처음에는 분명히 보이지 않은 채 서서히 쌓일 수 있다. ④ 근거 ❼❽ — 전자레인지는 가족이 함께 저녁을 먹는 일이 줄어드는 데 한몫했다. ⑤ 근거 ❺ — 전자레인지 이전에는 가족의 저녁을 만드는 데 오후의 상당 부분이 걸릴 수 있었다.
choice.psg: ❶ When we focus on the obvious aspects of media, we miss the changes that accumulate over time but are not apparent day to day. ❷ Most of us notice the obvious aspects of a new medium or technology while missing the more subtle aspects. ❸ Take, for example, the microwave oven. ❹ It was introduced in the early 1980s and revolutionized food preparation. ❺ Traditionally, one person spent the better part of an afternoon fixing an evening meal for a family. ❻ Now, it was possible to prepare foods very quickly, and this shortening of preparation time was liberating for the cooks in the family, most of whom tended to be women. ❼ But the short-term, obvious implications of greater convenience made it easy to overlook the long-term implications of no longer having one person fix food for the family to eat together at an evening meal. ❽ As time went on, fewer and fewer families sat down together to eat dinner. ❾ Meals that took a long time to prepare became a luxury of the past, except perhaps for special occasions. ❿ The effects of the microwave oven on family life were not anticipated and would have been difficult to foresee.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: were replaced by healthier recipes from earlier times
became an everyday part of most families’ routines
turned into something most families seldom had the time or habit to enjoy
came to be sold at very high prices in fancy restaurants
disappeared completely from every household in the world
choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 과거의 사치품이 되었다 → (특별한 경우가 아니면) 이제는 거의 누리지 못하는 것이 되었다 해설: 앞 문장 ❽ ‘점점 더 적은 가족이 함께 저녁을 먹었다’와 같은 문장의 ‘아마도 특별한 경우를 제외하고는’이 의미를 정한다 → 오래 걸리는 식사는 드물 게만 누리는 것이 되었다. ‘고급 식당에서 비싸게 팔림’은 luxury의 문자적 해석, ‘일상적인 부분’은 정반대, ‘모든 가정에서 완전히 사라짐’은 특별한 경우의 예외를 무시한 과장, ‘더 건강한 조리법으로 대체’는 무관. ① 예전의 더 건강한 조리법으로 대체되었다 ② 대부분 가족의 일과에서 일상적인 부분이 되었다 ③ 대부분의 가족이 즐길 시간이나 습관이 거의 없는 것이 되었다 ④ 고급 식당에서 매우 비싼 값에 팔리게 되었다 ⑤ 세상의 모든 가정에서 완전히 사라졌다
choice.body: As time went on, fewer and fewer families sat down together to eat dinner. Meals that took a long time to prepare became a luxury of the past, except perhaps for special occasions. The effects of the microwave oven on family life were not anticipated and would have been difficult to foresee.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) live (B) constantly (C) costly 근거 ❷❸❹❻ 해설: (A) ❸ real-time data → 실시간(live). outdated(오래된)는 반대. (B) ❹ continuously update → 끊임없이(constantly). rarely(좀처럼 ~ 않게) 는 반대. (C) ❻ 가동 중단 비용이 매우 클 때 일반화 → 고장이 큰 비용을 낳는(costly). trivial(사소한)은 반대. 요약문 해석: 디지털 트윈은 수년 동안 존재해 왔지만, 이제 빠른 연결망으로 전달되는 (A) 실시간 데이터 덕분에 센서가 그것을 (B) 끊임없이 업데이트할 수 있게 되었고, 이것이 고장 나면 (C) 큰 비용이 드는 기계에 그것이 점점 더 많이 쓰이는 이유를 설명해 준다.
choice.psg: ❶ Digital twins are digital replicas of assets or activities using modeling and sensors to create digital representations. ❷ Digital twins are not new; engineering teams in various industries have used 3D renderings of computer-aided design models, asset models, and process simulations for years. ❸ However, faster wireless networks and the resulting availability of real-time data enable much more detailed and dynamic digital representations. ❹ When sensors collect data from a connected device, the sensor data can be used to continuously update the digital twin. ❺ The digital twin becomes a real-time accurate copy of a physical object’s properties and states. ❻ For instance, digital twins of physical assets such as power-generation turbines, jet engines, and train engines are becoming common when the assets are very valuable and when downtime would be very costly.
choice.body: Although digital twins have existed for years, (A)________ data delivered over quick connections now lets sensors keep them (B)________ updated, which explains why they are increasingly used for machines whose breakdowns would be (C)________.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) long-established (B) accessibility (C) responsive 근거 ❷❸❹ 해설: (A) ❷ 디지털 트윈은 새로운 것이 아니며 수년간 사용되어 왔다 → 오래전부터 자리 잡은(long-established). unheard-of(전례 없는)는 반대. (B) ❸ the resulting availability of real-time data → 접근 용이성(accessibility). scarcity(부족)는 반대. (C) ❸ detailed and dynamic, ❹ continuously update → 즉각 반응하는(responsive). rigid(경직된)는 반대. 요약문 해석: 디지털 트윈이라는 개념은 공학에서 (A) 오래전부터 자리 잡은 것이지만, 달라진 것은 실시간 데이터의 (B) 접근 용이성이며, 이것이 이러한 디지털 버전을 예전의 시뮬레이션보다 훨씬 더 (C) 즉각 반응하는 것으로 만든다.
choice.psg: ❶ Digital twins are digital replicas of assets or activities using modeling and sensors to create digital representations. ❷ Digital twins are not new; engineering teams in various industries have used 3D renderings of computer-aided design models, asset models, and process simulations for years. ❸ However, faster wireless networks and the resulting availability of real-time data enable much more detailed and dynamic digital representations. ❹ When sensors collect data from a connected device, the sensor data can be used to continuously update the digital twin. ❺ The digital twin becomes a real-time accurate copy of a physical object’s properties and states. ❻ For instance, digital twins of physical assets such as power-generation turbines, jet engines, and train engines are becoming common when the assets are very valuable and when downtime would be very costly.
choice.body: The idea of digital twins is (A)________ in engineering, but what has changed is the (B)________ of real-time data, which makes these digital versions far more (C)________ than older simulations.

choice.stem: 위 글의 내용으로부터 추론할 수 없는 것을 고르시오.
opt: Digital twins are now cheaper to build than the physical assets they represent.
Earlier forms of digital representation existed before real-time data became widely available.
The value of an asset can influence whether a digital twin is built for it.
Better connectivity has helped digital twins become more detailed than in the past.
A digital twin depends on a steady flow of information from the object it represents.
choice.ex: ❻은 자산이 매우 가치 있고 가동 중단 비용이 클 때 디지털 트윈이 쓰인다고 할 뿐, 디지털 트윈과 실제 자산의 제작 비용을 비교하지 않는다(본문에 없는 비교). ① 근거 없음(정답) — 디지털 트윈은 이제 그것이 나타내는 물리적 자산보다 만드는 비용이 더 싸다. ② 근거 ❷❸ — 실시간 데이터가 널리 이용 가능해지기 전에도 초기 형태의 디지털 표현이 존재했다. ③ 근거 ❻ — 자산의 가치는 그것을 위한 디지털 트윈을 만들지 여부에 영향을 줄 수 있다. ④ 근거 ❸ — 더 나은 연결성은 디지털 트윈이 과거보다 더 상세해지도록 도왔다. ⑤ 근거 ❹❺ — 디지털 트윈은 그것이 나타내는 객체로부터의 꾸준한 정보 흐름에 의존한다.
choice.psg: ❶ Digital twins are digital replicas of assets or activities using modeling and sensors to create digital representations. ❷ Digital twins are not new; engineering teams in various industries have used 3D renderings of computer-aided design models, asset models, and process simulations for years. ❸ However, faster wireless networks and the resulting availability of real-time data enable much more detailed and dynamic digital representations. ❹ When sensors collect data from a connected device, the sensor data can be used to continuously update the digital twin. ❺ The digital twin becomes a real-time accurate copy of a physical object’s properties and states. ❻ For instance, digital twins of physical assets such as power-generation turbines, jet engines, and train engines are becoming common when the assets are very valuable and when downtime would be very costly.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: a printed photograph of the object taken on a single day
an outdated record that shows how the object looked years ago
a physical machine that can replace the original whenever it breaks
a backup file that protects company data from hackers
a digital version that shows the object’s present condition moment by moment
choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 실시간의 정확한 복사본 → 물리적 객체의 현재 속성과 상태를 매 순간 그대로 보여 주는 디지털 버전 해설: 앞 문장 ❹ ‘센서 데이터로 디지털 트윈을 지속적으로 업데이트한다’의 결과이므로, real-time accurate copy는 객체의 지금 상태를 매 순간 그대로 보여 주는 디지털 버전이다. ‘하루에 찍은 사진’은 copy의 문자적·정지된 해석, ‘몇 년 전 모습의 오래된 기록’은 real-time과 정반대, ‘원본을 대체하는 물리 적 기계’는 디지털을 물리적으로 바꾼 왜곡, ‘백업 파일’은 무관. ① 어느 하루에 찍은 객체의 인화된 사진 ② 객체가 몇 년 전에 어떤 모습이었는지 보여 주는 오래된 기록 ③ 원래 기계가 고장 날 때마다 그것을 대체할 수 있는 물리적 기계 ④ 회사 데이터를 해커로부터 보호하는 백업 파일 ⑤ 객체의 현재 상태를 매 순간 보여 주는 디지털 버전
choice.body: When sensors collect data from a connected device, the sensor data can be used to continuously update the digital twin. The digital twin becomes a real-time accurate copy of a physical object’s properties and states. For instance, digital twins of physical assets such as power-generation turbines, jet engines, and train engines are becoming common when the assets are very valuable and when downtime would be very costly.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) immediately (B) later (C) scarce 근거 ❷❸❹ 해설: (A) ❷ 최적의 장소를 찾아낼 뿐만 아니라 → 당장(immediately) 제공하는 것. eventually(결국)를 넣으면 not only A but B의 대비가 무너짐. (B) ❷ their future needs → 나중의(later). past(과거의) 필요는 반대. (C) ❸ 붉은 가문비나무가 이른 여름에 먹이를 적게 제공 → 부족한(scarce). abundant(풍부한)는 but plentiful과 대비가 성립하지 않음. 요약문 해석: 동물은 서식지가 (A) 당장 제공하는 것뿐만 아니라 그곳이 (B) 나중의 필요를 얼마나 잘 충족시킬지를 보고 서식지를 고르는데, 이는 처음에 는 먹이가 (C) 부족하지만 새끼가 부화하면 풍부해지는 곳에 자리를 잡는 한 명금류가 보여 준다.
choice.psg: ❶ The ability to select a set of surroundings suitable for foraging, shelter from predators, and the availability of mates is one of the most important determinants of biological success — measured as survival to reproductive age and the production of offspring. ❷ Many studies have shown that not only do animals have a remarkable ability to seek out the best available locations for the necessities of life, but that they are able to anticipate how a setting will serve their future needs. ❸ For example, the black-throated green warbler, a small songbird that nests in spruce forests of eastern North America, establishes territories preferentially among the red spruce trees early in the summer months, even though these trees offer less food than the neighboring white spruce trees. ❹ Later, though, when nests are built and hungry baby birds need nourishment, it is the red spruce forest that offers the easier pickings. ❺ Somehow, the warbler has been guided to settle in locations that will suit its future parenting needs better than its present ones.
choice.body: Animals choose habitats not only for what they offer (A)________ but for how well they will meet (B)________ needs, as shown by a songbird that settles where food is (C)________ at first but plentiful once its chicks hatch.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) thriving (B) predict (C) sacrificing 근거 ❶❷❸❺ 해설: (A) ❶ 생물학적 성공의 가장 중요한 결정 요소 → 번성(thriving). decline(쇠퇴)은 반대. (B) ❷ anticipate how a setting wil serve their future needs → 예측하다(predict). ignore(무시하다)는 반대. (C) ❸ 먹이가 적은데도 붉은 가문비나무를 고름, ❺ 현재보다 미래의 필요 → 현재의 편안함을 희생(sacrificing). demanding(요구하는)은 반대. 요약문 해석: 동물의 (A) 번성에 결정적인 요인은 환경을 고르는 솜씨이며, 연구는 동물이 장소가 자신에게 어떻게 도움이 될지까지 (B) 예측할 수 있고, 때로는 미래의 이익을 위해 현재의 편안함을 (C) 희생한다는 것을 보여 준다.
choice.psg: ❶ The ability to select a set of surroundings suitable for foraging, shelter from predators, and the availability of mates is one of the most important determinants of biological success — measured as survival to reproductive age and the production of offspring. ❷ Many studies have shown that not only do animals have a remarkable ability to seek out the best available locations for the necessities of life, but that they are able to anticipate how a setting will serve their future needs. ❸ For example, the black-throated green warbler, a small songbird that nests in spruce forests of eastern North America, establishes territories preferentially among the red spruce trees early in the summer months, even though these trees offer less food than the neighboring white spruce trees. ❹ Later, though, when nests are built and hungry baby birds need nourishment, it is the red spruce forest that offers the easier pickings. ❺ Somehow, the warbler has been guided to settle in locations that will suit its future parenting needs better than its present ones.
choice.body: A crucial factor in an animal’s (A)________ is its skill at picking surroundings, and research shows animals can even (B)________ how a place will serve them, sometimes (C)________ present comfort for future benefit.

choice.stem: 위 글의 내용으로부터 추론할 수 없는 것을 고르시오.
opt: Animals’ choice of habitat can reflect their needs at a future stage of life.
An animal may choose a place that seems less attractive at first.
The warbler’s choice of habitat pays off when its young need to be fed.
Where an animal decides to live can affect its chances of raising young.
The warbler learns from older birds which trees will provide food for its chicks.
choice.ex: ❺는 솔새가 ‘어떻게든(Somehow)’ 그런 장소로 유도되었다고만 하며, 그 능력이 어디서 오는지(학습인지 본능인지)는 말하지 않는 다(본문에 없는 원인 추정). ① 근거 ❷❺ — 동물의 서식지 선택은 삶의 미래 단계에서의 필요를 반영할 수 있다. ② 근거 ❸ — 동물은 처음에는 덜 매력적으로 보이는 장소를 고를 수도 있다. ③ 근거 ❹❺ — 솔새의 서식지 선택은 새끼에게 먹이를 주어야 할 때 결실을 맺는다. ④ 근거 ❶❺ — 동물이 어디에 살기로 하는지는 새끼를 키울 가능성에 영향을 줄 수 있다. ⑤ 근거 없음(정답) — 솔새는 어떤 나무가 새끼에게 먹이를 제공할지 나이 든 새들에게서 배운다.

trees whose fruit people can pick more easily
food that the parent birds can gather with less effort

Later, though, when nests are built and hungry baby birds need nourishment, it is the red spruce forest that offers the easier pickings. choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) conventions (B) assertively (C) tentative 근거 ❷❸❹❺ 해설: (A) ❷ 언어적 상호작용의 다양한 패턴과 양식을 배운다 → 관습(conventions). accidents(우연)는 ‘배운다’와 맞지 않음. (B) ❸ 개인주의 문화는 직접적·명시적, ❹ absolutely/certainly → 단정적으로(assertively). hesitantly(머뭇거리며)는 반대. (C) ❺ maybe, perhaps, probably — 암시적이 고 모호한 표현 → 조심스러운(tentative). forceful(강력한)은 반대. 요약문 해석: 아이들은 문화 특유의 상호작용 (A) 관습을 흡수하기 때문에, 개인주의 문화 출신의 사람들은 (B) 단정적으로 말하는 경향이 있는 반면, 화합 을 중시하는 집단주의자들은 (C) 조심스러운(잠정적인) 표현을 선호한다.
choice.psg: ❶ Language is a manifestation of culture. ❷ At different language acquisition stages, children do not learn language per se; rather they learn the various patterns and styles of language interaction that enable them to function as competent communicators in different situational contexts. ❸ They develop a culture-specific communication style that is, for example, direct and explicit in individualistic cultures or indirect and implicit in collectivistic cultures. ❹ Examples of words linked with the direct style are categorical words like absolutely, certainly, or positively. ❺ By contrast, the cultural assumptions of interdependence and harmony require that collectivists limit themselves to implicit and even ambiguous use of words, using terms like maybe, perhaps, or probably. ❻ The English language is the only language in the world that spells I with a capital letter. ❼ This phenomenon may reflect the fact that the roots of individualism are in England. ❽ There is no Japanese equivalent for the English I. ❾ Different words are used to refer to the self, depending on the social situation, the speaker’s gender, age, and the other social attributes relative to the listener.
choice.body: Because children absorb culture-specific (A)________ of interaction, people from individualistic cultures tend to speak (B)________, while collectivists, valuing harmony, favor (C)________ expressions.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

choice.body: The way English uniquely (A)________ the first-person pronoun may mirror its individualistic roots, while elsewhere the words people use for themselves (B)________ according to their social (C)________ to the listener.

choice.stem: 위 글의 내용으로부터 추론할 수 없는 것을 고르시오.
opt: Children in individualistic cultures learn to speak earlier than those in collectivistic cultures.
Words that express certainty are linked with a particular communication style.
A desire for harmony can make people avoid stating things too strongly.
Children learn how to communicate in ways that fit their culture.
How a person refers to himself or herself can depend on social factors.
choice.ex: ❷❸은 아이들이 문화에 따라 ‘다른 양식’을 익힌다고 할 뿐, 언어 습득의 ‘속도’를 문화별로 비교하지 않는다(본문에 없는 비교). ① 근거 없음(정답) — 개인주의 문화의 아이들은 집단주의 문화의 아이들보다 더 일찍 말하는 법을 배운다. ② 근거 ❹ — 확실성을 나타내는 단어는 특정한 의사소통 양식과 연결된다. ③ 근거 ❺ — 화합에 대한 바람은 사람들이 너무 강하게 말하는 것을 피하게 만들 수 있다. ④ 근거 ❷❸ — 아이들은 자신의 문화에 맞는 방식으로 소통하는 법을 배운다. ⑤ 근거 ❾ — 사람이 자기 자신을 지칭하는 방식은 사회적 요인에 따라 달라질 수 있다.

uses more capital letters than any other language

The English language is the only language in the world that spells I with a capital letter. This phenomenon may reflect the fact that the roots of individualism are in England.

choice.ex: (A) amplifier (B) thrilling (C) unbearable 근거 ❸❹❺ 해설: (A) ❸ 밀도가 올라감에 따라 기분과 행동이 강화된다 → 증폭기(amplifier). eraser(지우개)는 기분을 없앤다는 뜻이라 반대. (C) ❺ 두려워하는 행사는 경험을 훨씬 더 나쁘게 만든다 → 견디기 힘든(unbearable). tolerable(견딜 만한)은 반대. 요약문 해석: 혼잡성은 그 자체로 해롭다기보다 사람들이 가져온 기분이 무엇이든 그것의 (A) 증폭기 역할을 한다. 즉 신나는 행사는 더 (B) 짜릿하게, 두 려운 행사는 더 (C) 견디기 힘들게 만든다.
choice.psg: ❶ Environmental psychologists make a distinction between the physical measurement of density (how many people are in a particular space) and crowding (the psychological feeling of not having enough space). ❷ Usually, high density is needed for the phenomenon of crowding, which makes people experience sensory overload, a lack of control, and rising stress and anxiety. ❸ However, some psychologists see crowding as neutral rather than invariably negative, and believe that people’s moods and behaviors intensify as density increases. ❹ So if an individual is looking forward to a concert, say, the feeling of crowding enhances their enjoyment of the performance. ❺ But if they are dreading an event, crowding will make the person’s experience of it even worse. ❻ Put into a community setting, crowding may accentuate the dominant behavior — an aggressive group may turn violent as density rises. ❼ Conversely, creating positive social spaces such as parks and pedestrian areas in high-density urban environments may help to lift the general mood and defuse tension.
choice.body: Rather than being harmful in itself, crowding acts as an (A)________ of whatever mood people bring: it makes an exciting event more (B)________ and a dreaded one more (C)________.

calm down the most common behavior in a group
turn every crowd into a violent mob

para.en: When we focus on the obvious aspects of media, we miss the changes that accumulate over time but are not apparent day to day. Most of us notice the obvious aspects of a new medium or technology while missing the more subtle aspects. Take, for example, the microwave oven. It was introduced in the early 1980s and revolutionized food preparation. Traditionally, one person spent the better part of an afternoon fixing an evening meal for a family. Now, it was possible to prepare foods very quickly, and this shortening of preparation time was liberating for the cooks in the family, most of whom tended to be women. But the short-term, obvious implications of greater convenience made it easy to overlook the long-term implications of no longer having one person fix food for the family to eat together at an evening meal. As time went on, fewer and fewer families sat down together to eat dinner. Meals that took a long time to prepare became a luxury of the past, except perhaps for special occasions. The effects of the microwave oven on family life were not anticipated and would have been difficult to foresee.

Digital twins are digital replicas of assets or activities using modeling and sensors to create digital representations. Digital twins are not new; engineering teams in various industries have used 3D renderings of computer-aided design models, asset models, and process simulations for years. However, faster wireless networks and the resulting availability of real-time data enable much more detailed and dynamic digital representations. When sensors collect data from a connected device, the sensor data can be used to continuously update the digital twin. The digital twin becomes a real-time accurate copy of a physical object’s properties and states. For instance, digital twins of physical assets such as power-generation turbines, jet engines, and train engines are becoming common when the assets are very valuable and when downtime would be very costly.

The ability to select a set of surroundings suitable for foraging, shelter from predators, and the availability of mates is one of the most important determinants of biological success — measured as survival to reproductive age and the production of offspring. Many studies have shown that not only do animals have a remarkable ability to seek out the best available locations for the necessities of life, but that they are able to anticipate how a setting will serve their future needs. For example, the black-throated green warbler, a small songbird that nests in spruce forests of eastern North America, establishes territories preferentially among the red spruce trees early in the summer months, even though these trees offer less food than the neighboring white spruce trees. Later, though, when nests are built and hungry baby birds need nourishment, it is the red spruce forest that offers the easier pickings. Somehow, the warbler has been guided to settle in locations that will suit its future parenting needs better than its present ones.

Language is a manifestation of culture. At different language acquisition stages, children do not learn language per se; rather they learn the various patterns and styles of language interaction that enable them to function as competent communicators in different situational contexts. They develop a culture-specific communication style that is, for example, direct and explicit in individualistic cultures or indirect and implicit in collectivistic cultures. Examples of words linked with the direct style are categorical words like absolutely, certainly, or positively. By contrast, the cultural assumptions of interdependence and harmony require that collectivists limit themselves to implicit and even ambiguous use of words, using terms like maybe, perhaps, or probably. The English language is the only language in the world that spells I with a capital letter. This phenomenon may reflect the fact that the roots of individualism are in England. There is no Japanese equivalent for the English I. Different words are used to refer to the self, depending on the social situation, the speaker’s gender, age, and the other social attributes relative to the listener.

Environmental psychologists make a distinction between the physical measurement of density (how many people are in a particular space) and crowding (the psychological feeling of not having enough space). Usually, high density is needed for the phenomenon of crowding, which makes people experience sensory overload, a lack of control, and rising stress and anxiety. However, some psychologists see crowding as neutral rather than invariably negative, and believe that people’s moods and behaviors intensify as density increases. So if an individual is looking forward to a concert, say, the feeling of crowding enhances their enjoyment of the performance. But if they are dreading an event, crowding will make the person’s experience of it even worse. Put into a community setting, crowding may accentuate the dominant behavior — an aggressive group may turn violent as density rises. Conversely, creating positive social spaces such as parks and pedestrian areas in high-density urban environments may help to lift the general mood and defuse tension.
